newsitem.title: GERMANY: German building recovery seen only in 1998.
newsitem.headline: German building recovery seen only in 1998.

text.p: Germany's building sector will only start to recover in 1998 and both the former communist east and the economic dominant west will suffer investment falls through 1997, the country's building association said on Monday.

East Germany's post-unification boom fizzled out this year, and instead of meeting original expectations of investment growth of two percent this year, the final figure is likely to turn out showing a fall of between one and two percent.
That will lead to 30,000 job losses this year, and a 50 percent rise in insolvencies to a record 1,850, the association said in a statement.
During the first seven months of this year building orders fell by an "extremely disappointing" 7.4 percent in eastern Germany.
In the west the downturn in building business has continued in 1996. A fall in investment of four percent can be expected this year, causing 70,000 job losses, the association said.
Building orders fell by 7.9 percent in real terms in the first seven months of the year.
No turnaround is expected in 1997, and the falloff in business may become even more severe in the ex-communist east, with investment falling by four or five percent.
In the west, the fall should become less pronounced, with a fall of investment of two percent to be expected.
"The association only expects positive growth rates in 1998," the statement said.
